claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the stated baseline condition is a simple solid solution.
The simple-solid-solution state of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi lacks nanoscale chemical heterogeneity.
Baseline equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and compressive strength.
Baseline equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
A tailored thermal treatment or slight compositional adjustment can induce nanoscale chemical fluctuations or local ordering in CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale chemical fluctuations can contribute to increased alloy strength.
Local chemical ordering or nanoscale heterogeneities impede dislocation glide.
The untreated equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has low lattice friction.
Low lattice friction permits easy dislocation glide in untreated CoCrFeNiTi.
Easy dislocation glide causes the baseline alloy's favorable plasticity and reduced hardness and strength.
Introducing nanoscale heterogeneities raises local lattice distortion.
The induced heterogeneities increase the stress required for dislocation motion.
Thermally treated or compositionally modified CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly greater hardness than the baseline alloy.
Thermally treated or compositionally modified CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly greater compressive strength than the baseline alloy.
The strengthened material will retain acceptable ductility from room temperature to 600 °C.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and similar HEAs under quasi-static loading from room temperature to 600 °C.
The mechanism may not apply to far-from-equimolar compositions or dynamic and extreme loading conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as both 'as-cast' and 'homogenized,' while the baseline and experimental design specify a standard as-cast state. Homogenization is a post-casting treatment, so the controlled baseline state is ambiguous.
